newsitem.title: USA: Charlotte County, Fla., approves gasoline tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Charlotte County, Fla., approves gasoline tax hike.

text.p: Florida's Charlotte County Commission has approved a modified five-cents-a-gallon increase in the county's gasoline tax.

The county already levies a gasoline tax of six cents a gallon. Under the plan approved Tuesday, that will rise by one cent on Jan. 1, 1998. Additional two-cent jumps will take effect in January of 1999 and 2000 unless certain projects are complete by mid-1999.
Those include upgrading of hurricane evacuation routes, creation of a management plan to improve the county's public works and drafting of a budget for the planned Charlotte County Justice Center.
The tax will generate $600,000 a year for each penny added, or $3 million annually if the full five cents is added.
